**Fieldbook 2.2.1 beta 2** (a beta)
The second beta of 2.2.1, on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. Everyone else stays on 2.2.
### Changed - **Diagnostic reports show power and heat:** the activity log in **Help › Save Diagnostic Report…** now says whether the Mac was on battery or the power adapter, the battery level, Low Power Mode, and how hot it was running, at the start and end of each recording, while transcription runs during one, and whenever these change. It also says how long the speech model took to get ready.
### Fixed - **A light line around the sidebar on macOS 26:** the sidebar now reaches the window's edges, as on macOS 15 and 27, so its outline no longer shows on the style's color. - **The sidebar's bottom rows:** with a long customer list, **Opportunities**, **Licensing**, and **My To-dos** drew over the last customers. They now sit below the list, which scrolls above them.

**Fieldbook 2.2.1 beta 1** (a beta)
The first beta of 2.2.1, on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. Everyone else stays on 2.2.
### Changed - **Transcription keeps going while you record:** earlier meetings are transcribed, one at a time, during your next call, so their notes are ready sooner. **Settings › Transcription › Pause transcription while recording** (off) brings back the old wait, for a Mac that struggles during calls. - **Faster transcription:** part of the speech model now runs on the Neural Engine, about 10% faster, with slightly fewer words missed. The first transcription after updating takes a few extra seconds to prepare it. - **The Brief and the Detailed Summary:** the Brief is three to five takeaways for your team (what was decided, where things stand, what's next), even for a long meeting; the Detailed Summary is a full account of what was discussed, in order, with the names, numbers, and dates. - **AI that follows Your role:** with **Settings › General › Opportunities › Your role** set to Account Executive, the AI notes, account summary, pre-call brief, and next steps focus on budget, pricing, procurement, timeline, and who decides; as a Sales Engineer, on the customer's environment and requirements, as before. A recommended stage is suggested only for a Zscaler SE. - **Next steps for Salesforce:** **Write** now starts with an update line in your format, the date, your initials, and what happened ("10-14-26 - AJ - Met with customer, …"), then the open steps. **Copy** copies both. - **MEDDPICC from what the customer says:** your own questions and guesses in a meeting no longer count as evidence.
### Fixed - **A microphone switch during a call** could, rarely, leave the Recorder showing the microphone as interrupted after it came back, and the saved meeting warning that its audio was missing until the end.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything in the six betas of 2.1.2, which ships to everyone as 2.2.
### Added
- **Opportunities for each customer:** a new **Opportunities** row under **Account** keeps each deal you track in Salesforce or your CRM, stacked one per line like a folder's emails: click one to open it with its close quarter (such as **Q2 FY27**), **Technical Validation Stage**, Open/Won/Lost, a link that opens it in your browser, and your notes, with **Copy** on every section to paste into the CRM. **New Opportunity…** starts one in this quarter. **New Opportunity…** asks only for the name and close quarter; add the stage, link, and the rest on its page. - **The recommended stage and MEDDPICC per opportunity,** from the meetings that count toward it, its notes and your account notes, and the customer's emails. Each customer meeting has an **Opportunity** menu next to its Brief (where the stage menu was); while a customer has one open opportunity, its meetings count toward it on their own. - **Next steps:** **Write** suggests an opportunity's open next steps from the briefs and to-dos of its meetings (crossed-off to-dos count as done) and its notes, each linked to the lines behind it. - **Suggested opportunities** from the opportunities in your meetings' AI notes: **Add…** starts one with its name, and the meetings it came up in count toward it. - **Opportunities, every customer's at once:** **Opportunities** at the bottom of the sidebar, above **Licensing**, is a quick view of all your opportunities in one table, grouped by the quarter they close in: customer, opportunity, stage, status, close date, and amount, with each quarter's **pipeline** (its open opportunities' amounts; won ones have their own total). Click an opportunity's name to open it on its customer's page, or a quarter on the left to go to it. **Show won and lost** and **Copy as Table** (for a spreadsheet). - **Amount, close date, and forecast type on each opportunity:** an **Amount** in dollars (type 240000, $240k, or 1.2m), a **Close date** (it sets the close quarter), and **New** or **Upsell**. All optional, on the opportunity's page; amounts show on its line. They stay on this Mac: none of them is sent to the AI. - **Settings › General › Opportunities › Fiscal year starts in** (August unless you change it), for close quarters. - **Your role, SE or AE:** **Settings › General › Opportunities › Your role**, Sales Engineer (the default) or Account Executive. Selling Zscaler, an AE's opportunities show Salesforce's **Opportunity Stage** (0 - Pipeline Generation to 5D - Approved, awaiting processing) instead of the Technical Validation Stage, on each opportunity and on the Opportunities page; **6 - Closed Won** and **7 - Closed Lost** mark it won or lost, and marking it won or lost sets them. The recommended stage is for SEs. An SE's stage and an AE's are kept apart, so changing roles loses neither. - **Your own stages and an Opp ID for other companies:** with Microsoft Security or your own company in Settings › AI, an opportunity's stage is a text field you fill in, and an **Opp ID** field sits under its link (kept on your Mac, never sent to the AI). - **A licensing library:** **Licensing**, at the bottom of the sidebar above **My To-dos**, keeps your own SKU sheets, feature matrices, price lists, licensing guides, and vendors' licensing web pages, and answers questions about them, such as which edition includes a feature or what else is needed above 5,000 users. Each point links to the row or page behind it (**L1**, **L2**, …): click to see the row with its columns, then **Open File** or **Copy Row**. Nothing is built in: each SE adds what they use, once, and the library stays through updates. - **Add File…** takes Excel, CSV, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, or text, with the company it's about (sources are grouped by company). Spreadsheets are read one row at a time with their column names, up to 20,000 rows a sheet. **Replace…** brings in a newer version. - **Add Link…** reads a web page, or the page and the pages under it (up to 200), from this Mac when you add it, and keeps a dated copy; **Refresh** reads it again. Fieldbook reads links only when you add or refresh them, over HTTPS, and respects the site's robots.txt. A PDF that's a copy of a page with the same name isn't read again, and if a site has more, the source says how many links were left unread. - **Ask AI uses the licensing library too:** a question in the toolbar's search field about licensing (a license, edition, SKU, tier, add-on, pricing, or what something includes) also gets the best matching rows and pages of your licensing sources, cited as **L1**, **L2**, … beside the meeting lines. - **Share the library:** the **⋯** menu in the Licensing list has **Share Library…**, one file with every source, and **Import Library…** for one a colleague shared (or drop it on the list). Their sources join yours; ones you already have are updated only by a newer copy. - **Licensing in AI notes:** when you have licensing sources, a meeting's opportunities are matched to them after its notes are written: under each opportunity, the SKUs, editions, or add-ons that fit and what else they need, linked to the rows behind them. **Match Licensing** (or **Match Again** after your sources change) does it on request. - **A Zscaler SKU spreadsheet on request:** with **Zscaler** as your company (Settings › AI), the Licensing page says how to get a sanitized, pre-built SKU and features spreadsheet to add: email ajaw@zscaler.com (the address opens a new email). - **Set the side when you mark someone:** the **Who's talking?** box has a menu beside the name: **Internal**, **Customer**, **Partner**, or **Other**, also **Command-1** to **Command-4** while you type. It shows the side of the person you've chosen (an invitee or someone you've met) and starts as **Side** (not set) for a name you type; after the call, **Yes** gives the speaker that side. Clicking a mark in the meeting's header opens the box with its name filled in, so you can change just the side. - **Yes on a speaker mark sets the side too:** for a name you typed when marking, **Yes ⌄** under **Speakers** offers **Internal**, **Customer**, **Partner**, or **Other**, so one choice names the speaker and sets their side, without opening the speaker afterwards. A mark that knows the side (an invitee or someone you've met) shows it, as "Priya Shah (Customer)?", with a plain **Yes**. - **Remove a speaker mark made by mistake:** while recording, each mark in the meeting's header has a **✕**; after the call, so does its ⚑ line in the transcript, and the mark's row under **Speakers** has **Remove** next to Yes and No. Right-clicking a mark offers **Remove Mark** too. - **Change a mark's name while recording:** click a mark in the meeting's header to open **Who's talking?** again and choose someone else (or **No Name**); **Escape** keeps it as it was. - **Links in your notes:** web and email addresses in your meeting notes, account notes, and opportunities' notes are links: click one to open it in your browser, or point at it to see where it goes. - **Import transcripts from Word:** **Import Transcript…** and dropping a file now take `.docx` transcripts, such as Teams' **Download as .docx** (newer files with "Name 0:03" before each turn, and older ones with "0:0:0.0 --> 0:0:5.1" timings), with their speakers and times. The meeting's title, date, and length at the top and Teams' "started transcription" lines are left out. A Word document without times still becomes a manual meeting with its text in your notes. (`.txt` transcripts, including Zoom's export, were already imported.) - **The meeting being recorded, in the sidebar:** while recording, the meeting shows at the bottom of the **Recorder**, just above **Library**. Click it to go back to its notes after looking at a customer, a label, another folder, My To-dos, or Licensing. - **Keep or trash the .zip from your iPhone:** after a recording AirDropped from Fieldbook for iPhone is imported, a small **Imported from Your iPhone** window lists what came in and asks whether to keep the .zip files in Downloads or move them to the Trash. Several imports share one window, and while you're recording it waits until you stop. **Always do this** stops the question; change it in **Settings › General › Downloads**. - **Folders to the iPhone by themselves:** **File › Send Folders to iPhone…** now marks the file as coming from this Mac, so Fieldbook for iPhone (build 15 and later), watching its Downloads, uses each new one without asking once you've used folders from this Mac. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.2:** shown once after updating, with the two new places in the sidebar, **Opportunities** (with your fiscal year and **Show Opportunities**) and **Licensing** (**Open Licensing**), and what else is new since 2.1.
### Changed
- **Update All writes each account summary once:** while one of a customer's meetings is recording, being transcribed, or waiting for its automatic notes, its account summary is listed greyed out with what it's waiting for, instead of being written now and again when the notes arrive. An account summary that's up to date but would be changed by the meetings above it is listed as **Then, if the above change it**, so one run finishes the job instead of two. Update All's count leaves both out. - **Fewer AI requests after notes are written again:** the follow-up email is drafted automatically only with a meeting's first notes; afterwards your draft stays, marked as drafted before the notes changed, with **Redraft**. A meeting's licensing match is kept when its opportunities and your licensing sources haven't changed. - **The stage, MEDDPICC, and the recommended stage moved from meetings and the account to each opportunity.** The Account page starts with the customer's open opportunities, then account notes and the account summary. A customer whose meetings set a stage, or that had MEDDPICC, offers **Start an Opportunity with It…**, which brings both along. - **Update All** lists MEDDPICC per open opportunity, counting an opportunity's changes within a couple of seconds, and the pre-call brief uses the open opportunity's MEDDPICC. - **The account summary reads the customer's opportunities:** "Where things stand" names each open one with its close quarter and stage, using your notes on it; a statement that comes from an opportunity lists it among its sources. Adding or changing an opportunity (its stage, quarter, status, name, or notes) marks the summary out of date, so **Update** brings it up to date with just that opportunity, and removing one asks for a rewrite.
### Fixed
- **Update All's button counts again after a run finishes in the background:** closing its window while it works no longer leaves the button saying "Updated" until you open it and choose Done; once the run ends, the button shows what's still out of date. - **Rename Label and Rename Customer** show the name you're typing clearly: with a two-tone style it was light text on the box's white field.

**Fieldbook 2.1.2 beta 6** (a beta)
The last beta of 2.1.2 (added at the user's request for the AI savings), on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. 2.1.2 ships to everyone as **Fieldbook 2.2** (build 37), with everything from beta 1 to beta 6.

A meeting's licensing match is kept when its opportunities and your licensing sources haven't changed. - **Yes on a speaker mark sets the side too:** for a name you typed when marking, the mark's row under **Speakers** shows **Yes: Internal · Customer · Partner · Other**, so one click names the speaker and sets their side, without opening the speaker afterwards. A mark that knows the side (an invitee or someone you've met) shows it, as "Priya Shah (Customer)?", with a plain **Yes**. - **Add Link… reads up to 200 pages** under an address (was 50), so a whole site such as m365maps.com (104 pages, about 30 seconds) is read. Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update, a small one from 2.1. Everything in the two betas of 2.1.1.
### Added
- **Mark who's talking:** while recording, press **Control-Option-S** (from any app), click **Mark Speaker** in the meeting's header, or use the menu-bar icon, and type who it is in the small **Who's talking?** box (people invited and people you've met are suggested; your call app stays in front; its **✕** closes it without marking). After transcription, the speaker talking then is offered that name with **Yes** and **No** under **Speakers**; a mark without a name lets you listen from that moment and name them. The transcript shows where you marked. Marks made in Fieldbook for iPhone come with its recordings and are offered the same way. - **Cross off to-dos:** click a to-do's icon in a meeting's notes when it's done, or when it doesn't apply. It stays in place, struck through; click again to put it back. Completing a to-do's reminder in Reminders crosses it off too. - **Correct and add to-dos:** the pencil beside a to-do fixes its words, kind, or owner when the AI or the transcript got something wrong (**Use AI's Wording** undoes it). **Add To-do** adds your own, with **Remind me** to add it to Reminders right away. What you change is kept when the notes are updated or regenerated, and Copy, the follow-up email, Ask AI, the account summary, and the pre-call brief use your version. - **My To-dos:** at the bottom of the sidebar, your open to-dos from every meeting (the ones whose owner is you), grouped by customer, with a **Completed** list of what you've crossed off. Click one to open its meeting at that to-do. - **Azure OpenAI as a cloud service:** **Settings › AI › Cloud endpoint › Service › Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Foundry)** takes your resource's endpoint (or just its name; Fieldbook adds `/openai/v1` and shows where requests go) and one of its keys, kept apart from a LiteLLM endpoint's. Models are your deployments' names: if one isn't listed, choose **Other…** and type it.
### Changed
- **No more pauses from Update All's check:** working out what Update All can bring up to date now reads meetings' notes in the background, and only those that changed since the last check, so Fieldbook doesn't pause for a moment every couple of minutes or when you switch to it. The button's count also stays current while you record. - **The follow-up email and Ask AI check their sources:** as AI notes do, each point now comes with a few words quoted from the line it cites, and Fieldbook checks they're really there. In a follow-up email, a paragraph whose quote isn't found is asked about again once, and if it still isn't found it's marked with an orange warning for you to check before sending (the mark isn't copied). In an Ask AI answer, a citation whose quote isn't found shows as **not found** instead of a link. - **Fewer stray words split off to the wrong speaker:** in fast exchanges, a word at the start or end of a line could be credited to the person before or after and shown as a one-word line of theirs. Words are now grouped at pauses and given to speakers a phrase at a time, so a speaker changes only where someone says more than a word or two, and a short reply between pauses still keeps its own speaker. For new transcriptions and **Detect Speakers Again**.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything since 2.0, including what the four betas brought (they were called 2.0.1 while they were tested).
### Added
- **Release or Beta, for everyone:** **Settings › General › Updates › Versions** (and the top of the Welcome window) offers **Release**, tested versions for most people, or **Beta**, new features first while they're still being tested. With Beta, each beta comes as an automatic update, as well as every full release. Choosing Release again keeps the version you have until the next release. A beta shows which it is, such as "Version 2.1.1 beta 1". - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.1** opens once after updating: choose Release or Beta, and see everything new with where to find it. - **Emails for every folder:** customers, Internal, Training, Partners, and every label have an **Emails** row under **Files**: the folder's emails newest first, a reader with their attachments (a screenshot pasted into an email comes with them), **Open in Mail**, and an **Emails summary** linked to the emails behind each point. Click the open email's subject to fold it to one line. Add emails by dropping `.eml` files (Gmail's **⋮ › Download message**, or dragged from Mail or Outlook) or with **Add Emails…**. - **The email Inbox:** emails from your email folder (such as a Gmail label) wait in an **Inbox** instead of popping up, even during a call. The **Inbox** button at the top of the window, the Dock icon, and the menu-bar menu say how many; click it (or **File › Email Inbox…**, Shift-Command-E) to file each one as a new meeting or in a folder's **Emails**, where its people's domains suggest, in the background while you keep working. - **An email folder:** **Settings › General › Downloads and Email Folder › Email folder** watches a folder you choose, such as the Google Drive folder a Gmail label saves to, even while Fieldbook is closed. - **Emails become meetings:** drag an email from Mail or Outlook into Fieldbook, or download one from Gmail. The meeting is named from the subject and dated when it was sent, with who it's from and to and its text in your notes, the email and its attachments attached, and the folder its people's email domains point to chosen to begin with. - **Getting Emails into Fieldbook** in Help: every way to bring emails in, with step-by-step setup for a Gmail label (a script in a box that opens to show what it creates and does, with **Copy**), for flagging emails in Outlook with Microsoft 365 (a Power Automate flow), and for Apple Mail. - **The AI reads emails and attachments:** a meeting's AI notes read its attachments (emails, PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, and the words in screenshots, recognized on this Mac); a customer's MEDDPICC and recommended stage use its emails as evidence; **Ask AI** searches your folders' emails and can cite them; and emails kept in a folder's Files are read for the files summary, the account summary, and Account Discovery. - **Update All:** a button at the top of the window says how many AI notes, Discovery answers, MEDDPICC, and summaries have something new. Choose which to bring up to date (rewrites start unticked); they're done one at a time, sending only what's new where they can, and keep going when you close it. Anything that fails says why, with **Try Again** and **Try All Again**. Also **File › Update All…** (Shift-Command-U), and **Update <customer>…** on a customer's Account. - **Change a meeting's date and time:** click the date under its title, or right-click it in the list › **Change Date and Time…**. - **Drag a file into Fieldbook** to make a meeting from it, add it to a customer's Files, or attach it to a meeting: drop files anywhere in the window or on the Dock icon, or choose **File › Add Files…** (Shift-Command-A). A transcript becomes a meeting with its speakers and times; any other file becomes a manual meeting with the file attached and its text in your notes. Drop straight onto a customer in the sidebar or a meeting in the list, with **Undo**. - **Remind Me on to-dos:** click the bell at the end of a to-do to add it to Apple Reminders; the bell then shows when it's due, or **Done**. **New Reminder…** in a meeting's menu adds one for the meeting itself. - **Recordings AirDropped from the iPhone are imported by themselves** into the folder chosen on the phone, with **Undo** (Settings › General › Downloads), and **File › Send Folders to iPhone…** gives Fieldbook for iPhone your folders and the email domains that file meetings. - **Ask AI in Help:** type a question in Fieldbook Help's search field and press Return; the answer comes from the manual, with links to the sections it used. - **Microsoft Security** is back in **Settings › AI › Company and Solutions**, with its solutions list. Zscaler stays the default. - **Settings › Permissions lists the optional permissions** (Calendars, Reminders, the Downloads folder) with what each is for.
### Changed
- **A meeting's speakers are listed one per line,** most talk time first, with their side, whether their voice was recognized (or **Yes** and **No** for a suggested name), and how long they spoke. Click **Speakers** to fold the list. - **The account summary reads the account's emails and its meetings' attachments,** and **Update** sends just the new ones. Including the customer's other files stays your choice. - **The toolbar stays put:** **Notes | Transcript**, **Inbox**, and **Update All** are always in the same places, greyed out when they don't apply. - **Text size covers the meeting list and Help** too. - **The Welcome window is for anyone:** step 1 is **Bring your own AI**: Apple's on-device model, a local model, or a cloud model by API, with where Zscaler employees (their company's AI endpoint) and Microsoft employees (Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry, under **LiteLLM or OpenAI-compatible**; Help says how) get theirs. - **Recordings from the iPhone arrive filed** in the folder chosen there; one sent without its audio becomes a notes-only meeting; sending one again after choosing its folder moves the copy on the Mac; and dragging a meeting export into Fieldbook imports it without asking where it goes.
### Fixed
- **Imported Zoom files are dated when the meeting was,** from Zoom's file names, instead of when they were imported, and named **Zoom chat**, **Zoom transcript**, or **Zoom captions**. - **Long AI replies no longer fail:** notes whose reply runs past the AI's length limit are written from smaller parts of the meeting, an update that runs too long is written in full, and Discovery asks about a long document's questions in smaller sets. A customer's Discovery reads every document even when one fails, and says which. - **Links in Ask AI and Help answers aren't clickable;** only the citation chips open. - **New Customer, New Label, and Email Domains and Addresses are readable** in light mode with a dark sidebar.
